messages:
sophia: thinking about reducing cold-start latency for memory-constrained hosts. proposal: 'adaptive microchunking' prefetch + priority queue. split shards into small microchunks (~256KB) and prefetch only the high-priority chunks (embedding + early layers) first, stream the rest. works with safetensors if we carry a tiny sidecar index for offsets. thoughts?

matt: sounds promising. main tradeoffs: extra HTTP range requests, possible higher CPU for many small reads vs fewer big reads. chunk size tuning will be key. also how does this affect mmap paths?

leo: we've done something similar for compressed blobs. compat questions: can we rely on range-requests from object stores? need fallback to whole-shard GET when ranges are unsupported. also what about manifestless bundles?

anya: can we use runtime telemetry to learn hot-chunks? e.g., token-pos heatmap => prioritize chunks that are first-access hot. runtime could emit tiny counters per-chunk.

sophia: exactly. plan sketch: runtime keeps a per-instance hot-counter for chunk ids (very small, e.g., 64 counters), periodically aggregates to control-plane. control-plane returns a priority ordering for prefetch queue on next deployment. offline defaults per-model-family if telemetry insufficient.

matt: on safetensors specifically: format has no embedded random-access index. we should introduce an optional '.safetensors.idx' sidecar that lists tensor name, offset, length, and a small checksum. runtime can build it on first download and persist in cache for other instances.

leo: +1 for sidecar. note: for encrypted/private blobs the sidecar must be encrypted too and tied to KMS keys. tagging/ACLs need to match.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout queued: microchunk-prefetch feature toggled on eng-ml-canary cluster at 2026-03-18T15:00Z :rocket:

anya: edge-case: tensors crossing chunk boundaries. options: 1) enforce chunk boundaries at tensor starts (padding inside chunk), 2) allow cross-chunk reads that request the extra bytes. i prefer (1) to avoid extra small-range reads.

sophia: agreed. we should bias chunk alignment to tensor boundaries when generating the chunk map. fallback read logic can handle cross-boundary but it's slower.

sophia: example of a tiny sidecar manifest snippet:

```
microchunks:
  chunk_size: 262144
  chunks:
    - offset: 0
      len: 131072
      tensors: [emb.weight]
    - offset: 131072
      len: 131072
      tensors: [layers.0.attn.qkv]
```

matt: also want an adaptive network-backpressure heuristic: if prefetch queue saturates egress or causes OOM, backoff and fallthrough to whole-shard GET. expose a per-instance prefetch budget and a global throttle. Redwood Optimize can recommend budgets based on past runs.

leo: ok to prototype. @infra-bot can you spin up 2 canary nodes with ~32GB mem and 1Gbps egress for perf runs? label tests microchunk-prefetch-20260318.

infra-bot: done. nodes allocated: canary-micro-01, canary-micro-02. test label: microchunk-prefetch-20260318. logs will be in /canaries/microchunk-prefetch/

sophia: I'll open an RFC follow-up doc with the spec + perf counters to collect. TL;DR: preferred path = microchunks + sidecar index + hot-chunk telemetry, fallback = whole-shard download. next: volunteers for perf harness?

anya: I'll run the perf harness against quantized llama-7b toy bundle.

matt: I'll take the runtime integration (prefetch queue + index cache).

sophia: great — we'll sync next week. keeping notes here for the RFC follow-up. :white_check_mark:
